Findings.Claim: Every gap after Pending registry and finalizer registration, and before a verified BootExecute arm, becomes a truthful non-repeating Failed preparation.
Findings.Evidence: The power-loss form is true: the catch does not run, the task remains, and Finalize lines 954-972 convert a Pending or Running state with missing protection or a missing boot entry into Failed, zero verified bytes, NTSTATUS 0xC0000001, and an unregistered task. The exception form is false. Invoke-Prepare catch lines 786-806 remove BootExecute when armed and always call Unregister-FinalizerTask. They do not write registry Status. Initialize-MigrationRegistry has already forced Status 0 before Add-BootImage, the second boot readback, or Restart-Computer. A throw from any of those leaves Status Pending, no task, and no boot entry. Get-CurrentState then selects the Pending next action, Allow BootExecute to begin the raw copy at the next boot, which is false.
Findings.Impact: F stays read-only if protection already returned, and nothing copies or cuts over. The operator-visible status says a copy is armed. Nothing will run Finalize to correct that lie. Rerunning Prepare repairs it only if the operator does not trust the false next action.
Findings.Remediation: In the Prepare catch, after a registry key exists, write Status Failed, VerifiedBytes 0, and a failure NTSTATUS before unregistering the task. Status next text for Pending must also require bootImageArmed.

Findings.Claim: The native copy starts at byte zero, writes every source byte, flushes, rereads both devices, and records Verified only after that full compare. Terminal states skip disk I/O. Unknown status fails closed. Running restarts from zero.
Findings.Evidence: copy_blocks starts offset at 0 and rejects short geometry before device access. execute_migration checks bytes_processed against 210749095936, calls flush_destination, then verify_blocks with two buffers. VerifiedBytes, LastNtStatus 0, and Status 2 are written only after both checks, then NtFlushKey. A verify error returns before those writes, and run records Status Failed. decide_run maps 0 Start, 1 Restart, 2 SkipVerified, 3 SkipFailed, and any other value to Err. Skip paths return before NativeDevice::open. Restart and Start set VerifiedBytes 0 and Status Running before open. Read and write require the transferred length to match the request. PARTITION_INFORMATION_EX in Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 places PartitionLength at offset 16 and, with the RS3 IsServicePartition byte still aligned to an 8-byte union at offset 32, PartitionId at 48 and Attributes at 64. GPT_BASIC_DATA_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY is 0x1000000000000000, which is 1 shifted 60. The Rust reader uses those offsets and that bit. IOCTL_DISK_GET_PARTITION_INFO_EX is 0x70048.
Findings.Impact: A mismatch or short I/O cannot mark Verified. A later boot of a Running state recopies from zero.

Findings.Claim: Every Rust-visible Completed, Current, and Next line is truthful, including failure and panic.
Findings.Evidence: display_dashboard and display_operation_progress print the three labels from Progress. The restart preamble describes a reset to byte zero and is followed by clearing VerifiedBytes. SkipVerified says no disk I/O and points at the finalizer, and it returns before open. display_failure and the SkipFailed banner both end with: Boot Windows with the original F: mapping unchanged and read-only. display_failure is used for registry-open failure and for LayoutError::SourceNotReadOnly. The SourceNotReadOnly path has just proven the read-only bit is clear, so that Next sentence is false. SkipFailed prints it without opening the partition. The panic handler uses the same display_failure sentence after writing Status Failed.
Findings.Impact: Completed and Current on these paths identify the stage. Next can tell the operator that F is read-only when this boot image has either proved the opposite or has not looked. This does not by itself copy or cut over.
Findings.Remediation: Make the failure and SkipFailed Next text depend on a source read-only readback, or say that protection was not re-read.

Findings.Claim: Finalize cuts over only for Verified with exact bytes and NTSTATUS 0, and only after the source and target checks named in the acceptance list.
Findings.Evidence: Status 0 and 1 return before cutover. Status 3 restores the read-only F mapping and returns. Any other non-2 status throws after BootExecute removal and does not call cutover. Status 2 requires VerifiedBytes equal to SourceBytes and LastNtStatus 0. Cutover refuses a missing target or a writable source, checks the registry GUID, unmaps and offlines the old partition while leaving it read-only, temporarily mounts the target, checks ReFS and the label, resizes the partition to TargetFinalBytes when it is still clone-sized, requires the volume size to be at least final size minus 67108864, scans with Repair-Volume, checks Dev Drive by fsutil exit code, assigns F, rechecks partition identity and size, rechecks the old partition read-only, offline, and unmapped, rechecks the new volume, and then unregisters the task.
Findings.Impact: Pending, Running, Failed, and unknown cannot cut over. The 64 MiB volume floor still rejects an unexpanded source-sized volume. The partition size assertion is exact.

Findings.Claim: The 19 tests exercise real transfer, layout, progress, and status logic. Native orchestration gaps are source-inspection findings, not unresolved facts.
Findings.Evidence: Each test asserts a result: progress labels and replay, copy without verify or flush, flush error mapping, verify reads without writes, mismatch with flush_count 0, unaligned geometry before device access, decide_run for 0, 1, 2, 3, and 99, and layout rejection for a writable source, a wrong destination id, a read-only destination, and a wrong destination length. Cargo.toml sets the binary test flag false, so main.rs is not executed by cargo test. Uncovered but resolved by reading source: DuplicatePartitionIdentity is only reached when both expected ids are equal and both partitions have that id; the existing identity test returns DestinationIdentityMismatch first. SourceIdentityMismatch and SourceLengthMismatch have no direct test. Short native I/O, the registry checkpoint order, and the panic handler are in main.rs.
Findings.Impact: The library tests are genuine. They do not execute the boot entry. That does not leave an implementation fact unresolved.

Findings.Claim: The twelve power-loss statements in the review brief hold for power loss. The exception-path hole is A17, not a second power-loss hole.
Findings.Evidence: (1) Install-MigrationPayload does not create Pending or the task. (2) Protect runs before registry and task registration. (3) Protection readback is required before return. (4) Pending, finalizer readback, BootExecute readback, and reboot follow that return. (5) Finalize line 944 makes no protection claim. (6) Pending and Running read IsReadOnly and BootExecute. (7) A missing prerequisite records Failed, zero bytes, NTSTATUS 0xC0000001, removes an armed boot entry, unregisters the task, and does not copy. (8) Both true retains the retry and says so. (9) Power loss before Set-Partition in Protect creates no Pending key and no task, and F is not modified by earlier payload copies. (10) Power loss after a successful Protect return cannot clear IsReadOnly, because no later success or catch path sets source IsReadOnly false. Power loss before the registry write leaves no Pending task. Power loss after the task and registry write and before BootExecute leaves the task, and the next Finalize takes the A14 branch. (11) Rerun reuses an existing source-sized target, calls Protect again, overwrites Status with 0, replaces the task with -Force, and arms BootExecute. (12) No delete command exists.
Findings.Impact: The reported power-loss window is closed in source. A17 remains the exception-path state lie.
